fact: Cybernetica says that in 2014 it and the e-Governance Academy introduced an interoperability platform, known locally as Nam-X, connecting databases of different entities, and that Namibia has implemented it for secure data exchange between organisations.

Cybernetica says an ESTDEV-funded project begun in 2024 continues scaling the Nam-X platform, developing two digital services for it, and was expected to end in March 2025; no count of connected bodies is given.

The IISD report on a Global Partnership for Sustainable Development Data compendium says the e-birth and e-death notification platforms are linked to the National Population Registration System through the National Data Exchange Service Bus interoperability layer, which also lets the register link to other government and private-sector registers; no date for the link is given and the count of connected systems is not stated.

fact: The e-Governance Academy says its project, run October 2014 to December 2016, delivered an X-Road-based interoperability framework using Cybernetica's UXP technology to connect government databases, in three stages ending in full-scale implementation; it does not say the platform was in service.

fact: The World Bank blog says Namibia adopted the Estonian open-source X-Road software after 2011, so the National Population Register now links functional public and private sector registries, and it was used during COVID-19 to validate identity data for emergency income support.
The government is deploying NamX, a data-exchange platform for secure inter-ministry sharing, per UNDP Namibia.
